Thesis Research

Bachelor’s thesis · Andalas University · 2026

The Effect of Store Image on Customer Satisfaction through Perceived Value at Citra Swalayan Andalas Branch, Padang

Pengaruh Store Image terhadap Customer Satisfaction melalui Perceived Value pada Citra Swalayan Cabang Andalas Padang · Supervisor: Dr. Syafrizal, S.E., M.E.

This quantitative explanatory study examines how a store’s image shapes customer satisfaction, both directly and through the value customers perceive. It uses the S-O-R framework, Signaling Theory, and Expectation-Disconfirmation Theory, with data from questionnaires analyzed in PLS-SEM (SmartPLS 4).

153respondents
PLS-SEMSmartPLS 4
4/4hypotheses supported
Partialmediation

Research model — tap a hypothesis

Store Image
H1 → β 0.634
Perceived ValueR² 0.402
H2 → β 0.423
Customer SatisfactionR² 0.437
H3 · direct path, β 0.306

Who answered (n = 153)

Female 68%
Age 31–40: 32%
Students 39.9%
Shop 2–3×/month: 52.9%

Method: purposive sampling (the minimum under the 10-times rule is 80; 153 collected) via Google Forms with Likert scales; measurement and structural models evaluated with bootstrapping and PLSpredict.

Key findings

  • Store image has a strong effect on perceived value (f² = 0.672) and a smaller direct effect on satisfaction (f² = 0.099).
  • Perceived value partly explains how a good store image becomes satisfaction (indirect β = 0.268).
  • Highest-rated item: complete product selection (mean 3.92 of 5).

Implications & recommendations

  • Keep product range and friendly, helpful staff; improve store comfort, cleanliness, and uncrowded aisles.
  • Treat store improvements as a way to raise value perceived by customers, not only sales.
  • Future research: add service quality, customer experience, trust, and price fairness; use other retail types and a longitudinal design.

Limitations

  • R² values are in the weak range (0.25–0.49), so other factors also matter.
  • One store only, cross-sectional data, and self-reported questionnaires.
